name: La Bahia Hotel & Spa
positioning: Spanish-Mediterranean beachfront hotel and spa facing Santa Cruz's Main Beach, where the tip of Monterey Bay meets the town
best_for: Travelers who want a beachfront base between the Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk and the Santa Cruz Wharf
Spa-goers who want ocean views and outdoor treatment rooms
Travelers bringing a dog or cat

facts.text: La Bahia sits where the tip of Monterey Bay touches Santa Cruz's Main Beach.
The hotel faces Main Beach, with the Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk to the left and the Santa Cruz Wharf to the right.
The hotel is styled in Spanish-Mediterranean architecture.
The hotel's roots date back nearly a century, to oceanfront apartments and a hotel designed by architect William C. Hays.
The original bell tower was restored.
Guestrooms and suites have ocean views and pair a Spanish-Mediterranean aesthetic with a curated collection of worldly artifacts.
The Spa at La Bahia is inspired by Santa Cruz's original saltwater bathhouses.
The outdoor pool is heated and open year-round, with a hot tub.
High Tide is the hotel's signature restaurant, a Pacific Rim-inspired concept.
The resort fee includes complimentary beach cruiser bicycles and beach chairs, based on availability.
Dogs and cats are permitted for a per-stay fee.

highlights.text: The Moorish spa offers a steam room, an ocean-view sauna, a co-ed relaxation area, a Zen deck and outdoor treatment rooms above the sand and sea.
Beach butlers set up chairs, umbrellas and cooler bags on the sand for guests.
The Signature Suites are the largest suites, with ocean views, living and dining spaces and private furnished terraces.
The pool area has cabanas, fire pits and an infinity hot tub with views of the surf.
Guests can arrange surf lessons with local pro surfer Richie Schmidt.

considerations.text: Guests must be 18 or older to book.
San Jose Mineta International Airport is the closest major airport.
